notes: Confidence: observed -- every report line quoted, the four-case shapes and 'Overall Grade: A'; inferred -- the driver (the grader's tester did not survive: c4prj2_input/main.o is the student's main.c) and the two fixture decisions below (sorted remaining deck, fixed probe deck). Report wording observed verbatim in re/original-grade-txt/c4prj2_input.grade.txt: 'Compiling cards.c -> cards.o' (first of four compile lines), 'Linking input.o, future.o deck.o, cards.o, and our tester', the four-case 'Testing with input file with \n o <shape>\n o <unknowns>' labels, 'Your file matched the expected output', 'Test case passed', 'Overall Grade: A'. The four-case shape is reproduced by the case labels; the success lines read 'PASSED'/' - Correct' instead of 'Your file matched the expected output'/'Test case passed' because that wording is not expressible per case. The grader's tester did NOT survive: c4prj2_input/main.o is the student's own main.c (re/elf/c4prj2_input__main.o.md lists exactly its four section headers and no 'Testing with input file' strings), so drivers/c4prj2_input/input_check.c is INFERRED from that recovered main.c and exercises the same three functions the original linked: read_input, build_remaining_deck, future_cards_from_deck (from future.c). Test inputs: the original's own files were not preserved; the category-2/3/4 files are the student's own copies, whose contents match the original's descriptions exactly (test1.txt = 4 hands with no '?'; test2.txt = 4 hands with one '?0..?3' each; test.txt = 2 hands with '?0..?4' each), and category 1 (one hand, no unknown) is supplied on stdin because no such file exists in the directory (test3.txt has a '?11'). Two deliberate fixture decisions, to avoid over-constraining: the remaining deck is printed sorted by value/suit (card_from_num's mapping is explicitly the student's choice per the c2prj1_cards README, and an unsorted dump would pin it), and the future cards are drawn from a fixed card_from_letters probe deck rather than the unshuffled remaining deck, so what lands on ?0 depends only on future_cards_from_deck's documented contract. NOT memory-checked: c4prj2_input.grade.txt has no valgrind clause, so compile_and_run is used exactly as the 2024 grader did; leaks in read_input/add_future_card are therefore not detected here.
